Convert catboost model to party object

Source: R/catboost.Model.R
as.party.catboost.Model.Rd

Convert a single tree from a catboost boosted tree model to a party object for use with partykit visualization and analysis tools.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'catboost.Model'
as.party(obj, tree = 1L, data, ...)

Arguments

obj

A catboost.Model object from the catboost package.

tree

Integer specifying which tree to convert (1-based indexing, default is 1).

data

data.frame containing the training data with the response variable included (required). catboost models do not store the original training data or response values. The first column that is not a predictor is used as the response.

...

Not currently used.

Value

A constparty object from the partykit package.

Details

The tree structure is obtained by saving the model in JSON format via catboost.save_model() from catboost. Symmetric (oblivious) trees are expanded into a binary tree and branches that cannot be reached are removed.

Numeric splits send observations with feature <= border to the left child. One-hot categorical splits send the matching level to the right child.

Categorical splits based on target statistics (CTRs) are converted to factor splits using the approach described in extract_rules.catboost.Model(). When a CTR uses a combination of features, a factor with one level per combination is added to the data (named, for example, g:h) and the split uses that factor.

If the model was trained without feature names, predictors are matched to the columns of data by position.

Examples

These examples require the catboost package, which is not on CRAN. See the catboost installation instructions for details.

Fit a small model:

pool <- catboost::catboost.load_pool(mtcars[, -1], label = mtcars$mpg)
set.seed(3926)
fit <- catboost::catboost.train(
  pool,
  params = list(
    iterations = 3,
    depth = 2,
    thread_count = 1,
    logging_level = "Silent",
    allow_writing_files = FALSE
  )
)

Extract the rules for the first tree:

rules <- extract_rules(fit, tree = 1L)
rules

#> # A tibble: 3 x 3
#>    tree rules         id
#>   <int> <list>     <int>
#> 1     1 <language>     1
#> 2     1 <language>     2
#> 3     1 <language>     4

rule_text(rules$rules[[1]])

#> [1] "cyl <= 5"

Convert the first tree to a party object. The response is the first column that is not a predictor:

party_tree <- as.party(fit, tree = 1L, data = mtcars)
party_tree

#>
#> Model formula:
#> ~cyl + disp + hp + drat + wt + qsec + vs + am + gear + carb
#>
#> Fitted party:
#> [1] root
#> |   [2] cyl < 5: 26.664 (n = 11, err = 203.4)
#> |   [3] cyl >= 5
#> |   |   [4] cyl < 7: 19.743 (n = 7, err = 12.7)
#> |   |   [5] cyl >= 7: 15.100 (n = 14, err = 85.2)
#>
#> Number of inner nodes:    2
#> Number of terminal nodes: 3
